title: Waging War
coreMove: Price delay in real resources so you stop confusing drawn-out effort with disciplined pursuit of victory.
sourcePressure: The source counts the cost of campaigns in chariots, armor, silver, exhausted weapons, drained households, supply wagons, forage, rewards, and the danger of prolonged war.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the lesson into move fast at all costs or generic efficiency advice.

sourceAnchors.name: a thousand swift chariots
sourceAnchors.detail: The campaign cost is introduced through swift chariots, heavy chariots, mail-clad soldiers, provisions, armor, and silver per day.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Count the chariots before you admire the campaign; delay always sends a bill.

sourceAnchors.name: one cartload of enemy provisions
sourceAnchors.detail: One cartload taken near the enemy is treated as worth twenty cartloads hauled from home.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The best supply line is sometimes the one you no longer have to drag behind you.

hook: A battlefield metaphor imported into a modern office before the actual choice is visible
A generic sentence about strategy being planning under pressure
counterintuition: The obvious move is not always best; the opposite move is smarter
Winning is not about strength but about strategy
tryThisNow: Set a timer and think about your next battle
Write down your goal and one obstacle
examples: manager staring at a spreadsheet with a coffee cup

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches repeated phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes six examples feel like one example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a direct question, a tactical aside, a second-person passage, or a brief historical reference

exampleSpecs.domain: regional theater extending rehearsals for a troubled opening night
exampleSpecs.audience: artistic director with a fixed payroll
exampleSpecs.stakes: extra rehearsal weeks could save the show or bankrupt the season
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The empty ticket window at noon forces James to price each extra rehearsal day against the cash needed to keep the cast paid through closing weekend.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an empty ticket window under a faded poster

exampleSpecs.domain: medical-device recall held open while committees debate wording
exampleSpecs.stakes: every delayed day leaves clinics using questionable equipment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 6:40 a.m., Claire totals courier fees, call-center shifts, and replacement stock before forcing a recall decision that stops the daily bleed.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pallet of sealed replacement devices

exampleSpecs.domain: farm co-op choosing whether to repair a broken grain dryer or rent one now
exampleSpecs.stakes: wet grain loses value every day while members argue about capital expense
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: How expensive is the cheap delay if every truckload loses grade by Friday?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: kernels stuck to a damp sample bag

exampleSpecs.domain: university lab stuck in a months-long equipment procurement dispute
exampleSpecs.stakes: the grant clock is burning while the team waits for perfect terms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The freezer alarm chirps while Ingrid marks each lost week against expiring samples and chooses a shorter lease that preserves the experiment.

exampleSpecs.domain: independent restaurant keeping a failing lunch service alive
exampleSpecs.stakes: staff hours and food waste are draining the profitable dinner business
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Marco twelve trays of unsold focaccia to see that pride in the lunch menu was consuming the dinner engine.

exampleSpecs.domain: software migration where parallel systems run too long
exampleSpecs.audience: program manager at a pension administrator
exampleSpecs.stakes: dual operations double error checks and exhaust the support team
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Name the shutdown date before we approve another bridge, Layla tells the steering group, then lists every duplicate control running because nobody will end the campaign.

skillTargets: spot hidden carrying costs in delay
choose resource capture over repeated resupply
